historical_references.reference: Muad ibn Jabal was an early convert to Islam and one of the ten companions of the Prophet Muhammad who were given the title 'Ashab Al-Siddiq.' He was a scribe and was known for his excellent calligraphy. Muad became a close friend of the Prophet and was given the responsibility of writing the first copy of the Quran on parchment. This was during the second caliphate of Umar ibn Al-Khattab (634-644 AD).

historical_references.reference: Muad ibn Daniqal was a companion of Prophet Muhammad and served as the chief scribe of the Islamic state under the first caliph, Abu Bakr As-Siddiq. He was responsible for recording the conquests and treaties of the expanding Islamic empire. Muad is also known for his role in the Battle of Hunayn (630 AD), where he was a standard-bearer for the Prophet.
